To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the path amplitudes of millimeter wave channels at 28 GHz are Rician distributed with K-factor ranging between 3 and 15 dB, the average spatial correlation of individual multipath amplitudes reaches a value of 0 after approximately 5 wavelengths, and the path delays are distributed uniformly between 1 and 5 nanoseconds.

the path amplitudes of the 28 GHz millimeter-wave channels measured in this study follow a Rician model, with K-factor values in the range of 3-15 dB for both co- and cross-polarized antennas, and that the path gain spatial autocorrelation function decays to zero after a few wavelengths.

the path gains in the millimeter- wave band are correlated over a short distance, but the spatial correlation length is much shorter than that of the centimeter wave band, and the path gains follow a Rician fading model.
